subject: Banking
title: The AOL-Time Warner Merger
description: A quick win: understand The AOL-Time Warner Merger.

hook.text: In 2000, AOL bought Time Warner for $164 billion. It was the largest merger in history.

buildup.text: AOL was an internet company with inflated stock. Time Warner had real media assets.

discovery.text: The dot-com bubble burst shortly after. AOL's stock price collapsed, dragging the combined company into massive losses.

twist.text: By 2002, the company wrote off $99 billion. It was the largest corporate write-off in American history at the time.

climax.text: AOL-Time Warner proved that merging hype with substance creates neither. The deal destroyed a century of media legacy.

punchline.text: $164 billion deal, $99 billion written off. The worst merger ever.

quiz.question: Why did the AOL-Time Warner merger fail so badly?
options: The dot-com bubble burst and AOL's inflated stock value collapsed
